doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Moving to New York and living in a nurses' residence
summary: His first weeks in New York were spent in a hospital nurses' residence.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I mean you’d had it in your head for a while at this point that you had to get to New York?
Sure. Unquestionably. So much so that the first three weeks that I lived there I lived in the nurse’s residence at Columbia Presbyterian Hospital in Port Washington.

I don’t want to really go into detail about that. It was the only option I had to get my foot in the Manhattan door. So I did. I just think it’s funny walking past the nurse’s station with my bass every night, with the little like front desk they had, because it was like a dormitory.
Well good story. You know, years later it makes for a good story.
